rundown: Patriots beat Roos 76-68 at McArthur Center in St. Petersburg, FL. Patriots led 37-33 at half-time and never looked back. By ESPN's win probability it was never really in doubt (never below 76%).
Leading the way — Roos: Jaylen Smith 22 pts, 3 ast; Assane Diop 6 reb. Patriots: Shane Pendergrass 16 pts; Brayden O'Connor 6 ast; Baraka Okojie 7 reb.
Where Patriots won it: they shot 50% to 46%, won the boards 32-24 and had 12 assists to 10.
Against the closing line (Draft Kings): Patriots closed as 15.5-point favorites and won but didn't cover (Roos +15.5 cashed); the total closed at 141.5 and they combined for 144, over by 2.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 12, 2:53 PM ET. It had Roos 20% and Patriots 80%, projecting Roos 72.9 – Patriots 82.3 (155.2 total, Patriots by 9.3).

Final: Roos 68 – Patriots 76. Right winner: it had Patriots at 80%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Roos came in with a 5% below average attack and a 2% leakier than average defense (2-2, 77.3 scored and 78.3 allowed a game over 4 games), worth about 179 and 177 games of evidence. Projected to score 72.9, they scored 68 (−4.9 points, 7% under); projected to allow 82.3, they allowed 76 (−6.3 points, 8% under).

Patriots came in with a league-average attack and a 6% stingier than average defense (2-0, 75 scored and 52.5 allowed a game over 2 games), worth about 165 and 163 games of evidence. Projected to score 82.3, they scored 76 (−6.3 points, 8% under); projected to allow 72.9, they allowed 68 (−4.9 points, 7% under).

The bigger miss was Patriots' scoring (-6.3 points against projection); both sides underscored their projections, so the game ran colder than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 144 against 155.2 projected (-11.2), about the 22nd percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±14.5).

Margin: Patriots by 8 against Patriots by 9.3 projected, about the 45th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±11).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

OVER 141.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 52% vs 50% fair (+2.5 pts), THE PICK — won (+0.9u); same number as the close. UNDER 141.5 (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 48% vs 50% fair (-2.5 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

review.title: Where the public and the money were
review.body: Splits (Action Network): spread: 16% of bets on Roos, 25% of the money — Roos covered; total: 81% of bets on the over, 54% of the money — it went over; moneyline: 5% of bets on Roos, 15% of the money.

review.title: What could have made it wrong

Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin.

The projection landed within its normal range anyway, so the flags didn't cost it much this time.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.927 of the raw projection. It counts toward CBB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 405 graded CBB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.998 and gives home teams +1.1 points. Team corrections so far: Roos attack ×1.017, defense ×1.005 (4 games).

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, the pick won (+0.9u).
